_provenance.generated_by: Wright-Fisher simulation of neutral drift vs directional selection
_provenance.data_origin: Analytical: Wright-Fisher model with known fixation probabilities. Drift dominance threshold from population genetics theory (Kimura 1968). No external datasets.

_description: Wright-Fisher simulation testing when stochastic drift dominates over deterministic selection in finite populations. Connects to R. Anderson's finding that drift dominates in low-biomass subseafloor habitats.
_groundspring_question: When does noise (drift) overwhelm signal (selection) in an evolving system? The answer depends on N_e × s — the product of effective population size and selection coefficient. This is the biological analog of signal-to-noise ratio.
_cross_spring: wetSpring — microbial diversity; Exp 004 sequencing depth (rare biosphere detection limit)

model._description: Wright-Fisher model: N diploid individuals, allele A has fitness 1+s relative to allele a (fitness 1). Initial frequency p₀=0.5. Simulate until fixation or loss. Track fixation probability and diversity trajectory.

analytical_predictions._description: Kimura (1968): fixation probability under selection is P_fix = (1 - exp(-2s)) / (1 - exp(-2Ns)). For neutral (s=0): P_fix = 1/2N (with p₀=1/2N) or p₀ (with initial freq p₀). When N*s >> 1: selection dominates. When N*s << 1: drift dominates.
